item.title: Joe Jonas Says He Sought Therapy After His Solo Album Underperformed
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to this week's episode, where we're diving into the world of music and mental health. You might know him as a member of the Jonas Brothers, but Joe Jonas has been open about his struggles with the pressures of fame. Let's take a listen.
[Soft music transitions]
Host: Back in 2011, Joe Jonas released his solo debut album, Fastlife. But despite his expectations, the album didn't quite live up to his hopes. It peaked at number 15 on the Billboard 200, and its lead single "See No More" only reached number 92 on the Hot 100.
[Pause for emphasis]
Host: Joe Jonas has revealed that this disappointing commercial performance triggered panic attacks and physical pain. He even sought medical attention, but was told he was physically healthy and should consider therapy. At first, he resisted the idea, but eventually found himself taking long bike rides to escape his phone and clear his head.
[Short music transition]
Host: But Joe Jonas didn't give up on music. In 2015, he formed the funk-pop band DNCE, and their debut single "Cake by the Ocean" became a mainstream hit, reaching number 9 on the Billboard Hot 100. And when the Jonas Brothers reunited in 2019, they topped the Billboard 200 with their album Happiness Begins, featuring the number 1 single "Sucker".
[Outro music plays]
Host: It's a powerful reminder that even in the face of disappointment and pressure, there's always a second chance to find success and happiness. Thanks for tuning in to this week's episode, and we'll catch you next time.
